parsed.rationale: V1–V4 show QS complexes with about 2.5–3 mm coved ST elevation in V2–V3 and at least 1 mm in V1/V4, which meets STEMI criteria. QRS is narrow in the limb leads and V6, so this is not LBBB. The established Q waves and deep T inversions could point to an evolving (late-presenting) anterior MI or an old anterior MI with an LV aneurysm rather than a hyperacute one, so the clinical history, symptom timing and serial ECGs and troponins should guide management.
